CENTENNIAL, Colo.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Quantum Corporation (Nasdaq: QMCO) ("Quantum" or the "Company"), today announced financial results for its fiscal second quarter of 2027 ended September 30, 2026.


**Fiscal Second Quarter 2027 Financial Summary**


- Revenue increased sequentially and 42.9% year-over-year to $89.6 million, with strong customer demand also contributing to record order backlog
- Gross margin expanded to 41.0%, increasing 170 basis points sequentially and 340 basis points year-over-year
- GAAP operating expenses were $29.9 million; non-GAAP adjusted operating expenses were $26.9 million
- GAAP net loss was $44.8 million, or ($1.14) per share, which included a $51.6 million non-cash adjustment from the change in fair value of warrant liabilities
- Non-GAAP adjusted net income increased to $9.8 million, or $0.25 per share
- Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA was $11.1 million


“This quarter marked our fourth consecutive quarter of sequential revenue growth and our second quarter of non-GAAP profitability. These results underscore the meaningful progress we have made over the past year in strengthening execution, improving our financial position, and positioning Quantum for sustainable growth,” commented Hugues Meyrath, Chief Executive Officer of Quantum. “Revenue grew 42.9% year-over-year and 11% sequentially to more than $89.6 million, driven by strong demand across our secondary storage portfolio. We ended the quarter with a record backlog of nearly $100 million, and we also secured one of the most significant purchase orders in the Company’s history — a major hyperscale deployment of our Scalar i7 Raptor following a multi-year evaluation in which reliability, density, and infrastructure efficiency were key differentiators. Additionally, we closed the largest ActiveScale Cold Storage order in company history, nearly doubling the number of core transactions above $500,000.”


“Tape remained our most consistent growth driver with hyperscale demand increasing more than 2.6 times year-over-year as customers recognize tape’s strategic role in addressing AI-driven infrastructure strain. Although supply constraints continue to affect shipment timing in certain areas, our ability to secure disk drives has improved, enabling us to fulfill previously delayed orders as demand remains ahead of available supply. With the recent introduction of Quantum Autonomous Data Management (ADM), which combines intelligence with action and is tightly integrated with ActiveScale and our tape portfolio, we are helping customers optimize data placement based on value, risk, and cost. Combined with expanding opportunities across hyperscale, enterprise, government, and critical-infrastructure customers, we are well positioned to capitalize on accelerating data growth driven by AI, analytics, compliance, and cyber-resilience requirements.”


**Fiscal Second Quarter 2027 vs. Prior Year Fiscal Quarter**


Revenue for the fiscal second quarter of 2027 was $89.6 million, compared to $62.7 million in the prior year second quarter, an increase of 42.9%. GAAP gross profit in the fiscal second quarter of 2027 was $36.7 million, or 41.0% of revenue, compared to $23.6 million, or 37.6% of revenue, in the fiscal second quarter of 2026.


Total GAAP operating expenses in the fiscal second quarter of 2027 were $29.9 million, or 33.4% of revenue, compared to $31.7 million, or 50.6% of revenue, in the prior year. Total operating expenses on a non-GAAP basis for the fiscal second quarter of 2027 were $26.9 million, compared to $24.8 million in the fiscal second quarter of 2026.


GAAP net loss in the fiscal second quarter of 2027 was $44.8 million, or $(1.14) per share, compared to a net loss of $46.5 million, or $(3.49) per share, in the fiscal second quarter of 2026. The second quarter net loss includes a charge of $51.6 million related to our outstanding warrants.


Excluding the change in fair value of warrant liabilities, special project costs, and stock-based compensation, non-GAAP adjusted net income in the fiscal second quarter of 2027 was $9.8 million, or $0.25 per share, compared to adjusted net loss of $7.1 million, or ($0.54) per share, in the prior year second quarter.


Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA in the fiscal second quarter of 2027 was a positive $11.1 million, compared to positive $0.5 million in the fiscal second quarter of 2026.


For a reconciliation of GAAP to non-GAAP financial results, please see the financial reconciliation tables below.


**Liquidity and Debt** (as of September 30, 2026)


- Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash were $67.5 million, compared to $16.2 million as of the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026
- The Company had no outstanding debt at quarter-end and incurred no interest expense during the fiscal second quarter, compared to outstanding term loan debt, excluding debt issuance costs, of $55.9 million, and $2.9 million of interest expense in the fiscal fourth quarter of 2026


**Business Outlook**


Fiscal third quarter 2027 guidance is as follows:


- Revenue of $91.0 million, plus or minus $2 million
- Non-GAAP adjusted operating expenses of $28 million, plus or minus $1 million
- Non-GAAP adjusted basic net income per share of $0.20, plus or minus $0.10
- Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA of $9.1 million, plus or minus $1 million


This assumes an effective annual tax rate of 3%; non-GAAP adjusted net income per share assumes an average basic share count of approximately 39.5 million in the fiscal third quarter of 2027.


The Company cannot reconcile its non-GAAP guidance to the most directly comparable GAAP measures without unreasonable efforts because it cannot reliably predict warrant fair value changes, which depend on its future stock price, or the timing and amount of restructuring charges, special project costs and stock-based compensation expense. These items could materially affect GAAP results.

**About Quantum**


Quantum delivers end-to-end data management solutions designed for the AI era. With over four decades of experience, our data platform has allowed customers to extract the maximum value from their unique, unstructured data. From high-performance ingest that powers AI applications and demanding data-intensive workloads, to massive, durable data lakes to fuel AI models, Quantum delivers the most comprehensive and cost-efficient solutions. Leading organizations in life sciences, government, media and entertainment, research, and industrial technology trust Quantum with their most valuable asset – their data. For more information, visit[www.quantum.com](http://www.quantum.com/) .

**NON-GAAP FINANCIAL MEASURES**


To provide investors with additional information regarding our financial results, we have presented certain non-GAAP financial measures in this press release, including non-GAAP adjusted operating expenses, non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA, non-GAAP adjusted net income (loss) and non-GAAP adjusted net income (loss) per share.


Non-GAAP adjusted operating expenses is a non-GAAP financial measure defined by us as GAAP operating expenses with stock-based compensation expense, restructuring charges, amortization of acquisition related intangible assets and other special project costs removed. Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA is defined by us as GAAP net income (loss) excluding interest expense, net, provision for income taxes, depreciation expense, amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets, stock-based compensation expense, restructuring charges, (gain) loss on debt extinguishment, change in fair value of warrant liabilities, change in fair value of convertible note and other special project costs. Non-GAAP adjusted net income (loss) is defined by us as GAAP net income (loss) excluding the same items, other than interest expense, net, provision for income taxes and depreciation expense, and non-GAAP adjusted net income (loss) per share is non-GAAP adjusted net income (loss) divided by weighted average shares outstanding.


We have provided below reconciliations of each non-GAAP financial measure to the most directly comparable U.S. GAAP financial measure. Management uses these non-GAAP financial measures to evaluate operating performance and prepare internal budgets and forecasts. We believe that the exclusion of the amounts eliminated in this calculation can provide a useful measure for period-to-period comparisons of our core business performance. Accordingly, we believe that the use of non-GAAP financial measures provide useful information to investors and others in understanding and evaluating our operating results in the same manner as our management and our board of directors.


Our use of non-GAAP financial measures have limitations as analytical tools, and you should not consider them in isolation or as a substitute for analysis of our financial results as reported under U.S. GAAP.


Other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate non-GAAP financial measures differently, which reduces their usefulness as comparative measures. Because of these and other limitations, you should consider non-GAAP adjusted operating expenses, non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA, non-GAAP adjusted net income (loss) and non-GAAP adjusted net income (loss) per share, along with other U.S. GAAP-based financial performance measures, including various cash flow metrics and our U.S. GAAP financial results.
